intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Ukraine's refinery strikes raise food aid fears
items.text: Ukraine has hit at least 14 Russian oil refineries since early November, despite a request from President Trump to stop. President Putin has said Russia will take retaliatory measures. Zelensky has defended the strikes. Meanwhile, the World Food Programme has warned that the war is disrupting grain shipments. It says food aid for 7.3 million people is now at risk. In Odesa region, a Russian strike killed two people and injured three, including a child.

gloss.refinery: a factory where crude oil is turned into fuel
gloss.retaliatory: done to hit back at an attack
gloss.defend: to say that something is right or justified
gloss.disrupt: to interrupt something so that it cannot continue normally
gloss.at risk: in danger of being harmed or lost

items.title: Iowa plans huge blast at ammunition plant
items.text: The US Army has prepared to destroy nearly five tons of lead azide, an explosive chemical, at an ammunition plant near Middletown, Iowa. Governor Kim Reynolds has declared a disaster emergency in three counties. Officials recommended that people leave Middletown and a five-mile area to the south-west. People up to 20 miles away were told to stay indoors. An Army map shows that lead dust could drift more than 100 miles, as far as northern Missouri.

gloss.detonate: to make a bomb or explosive go off
gloss.disaster emergency: an official state of crisis that allows extra help
gloss.plume: a long cloud of smoke or dust rising from a place
gloss.drift: to be carried slowly by wind or water

items.title: Unilever cuts Channel 4 advertising by 92%
items.text: Unilever has cut about 92 per cent of its advertising spending with Channel 4, the Guardian reported on 24 November. The company is also reducing its UK television budget, which was close to £100 million, by more than half compared with last year. Unilever is moving more of its money towards influencer marketing, where social media personalities promote products. The change is a blow for traditional broadcasters, which depend on advertising income to pay for programmes.

gloss.spending: money that is used to pay for things
gloss.budget: the amount of money planned for a particular purpose
gloss.influencer: a person with many social media followers who promotes products
gloss.depend on: to need something in order to survive
gloss.broadcaster: a company that sends out TV or radio programmes

items.title: Isak scores twice as Liverpool beat Brugge
items.text: Liverpool won 3-0 at Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday. Alexander Isak scored in the 13th minute to give the visitors an early lead. Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 in the 79th minute. Isak then added a second goal three minutes later to finish the match. The result was a comfortable night for Liverpool, who did not concede a goal. Elsewhere, Paris Saint-Germain drew 2-2 with Roma, which ended their run of 12 wins.

gloss.concede: to let the other team score a goal
gloss.comfortable: easy, without much difficulty or worry
gloss.end a run: to stop a series of wins or successes
gloss.visitors: the team playing away from home
gloss.draw: to finish a match with the same score for both teams

items.title: Czechia reach Davis Cup semi-finals
items.text: Czechia have reached the semi-finals of the Davis Cup Finals after beating Canada 2-0. Tomas Machac won the first match against Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2. Jiri Lehecka then defeated Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6, 6-2 to win the tie. Lehecka saved all nine break points he faced. He had lost his last three meetings with Auger-Aliassime, but this win cut the deficit to 2-3. Lehecka said it was a very tough match.

gloss.tie: a match between two countries made up of several games
gloss.break point: a chance to win a game when your opponent is serving
gloss.save: to stop the opponent from winning a point
gloss.deficit: the amount by which one side is behind
gloss.clinch: to win something in a way that cannot be changed

items.title: Meta brings Muse AI assistant into Instagram
items.text: Meta has added its AI assistant, Muse, directly to Instagram direct messages, TechCrunch reported on 24 November. Users can now chat with the assistant inside their private conversations. Meta has also teamed up with Walmart so that Muse can help shoppers find Black Friday deals. The move is part of a wider push by large technology companies to put AI tools in the apps that people already use every day.

gloss.assistant: a computer program that helps users do tasks
gloss.team up: to join with another person or company to work together
gloss.direct message: a private message sent to one person or a small group
gloss.push: a strong effort to achieve or promote something
gloss.shopper: a person who buys things in shops or online

items.title: Few heart attack patients get a flu jab
items.text: A Swedish study has found that only 6 per cent of heart attack patients received a flu vaccine in hospital, even though guidelines recommend it. Researchers at Örebro University studied patients and found that those who were vaccinated had a 41 per cent lower risk of death in the following year. The study was published in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe. It is observational, so it shows a link but cannot prove that the vaccine caused the benefit.

gloss.flu jab: an informal British word for a flu vaccination
gloss.guidelines: official advice about how something should be done
gloss.observational: based on watching what happens, not on a controlled experiment
gloss.vaccinate: to give someone a vaccine to protect them from disease

items.title: A24 box office passes $526 million
items.text: The film studio A24 has taken more than $526 million at the US box office this year, up to 15 November, CNBC reported. That is more than 50 per cent above its total for the whole of 2025. The studio's success has been driven by the horror film Backrooms, the romance The Drama and the Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything. A24 is known for independent films with a distinctive style.

gloss.box office: the money earned from cinema tickets
gloss.drive: to be the main cause of something's success or growth
gloss.documentary: a film that gives facts about real events or people
gloss.distinctive: clearly different and easy to recognise
gloss.independent: made without money or control from a big studio

items.title: US inflation rises to highest since 2023
items.text: Inflation in the United States has accelerated, SBS News reported on 26 November. The growth of the personal consumption expenditures price index rose in October. Core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, reached its highest level since 2023. Prices are moving further from the Federal Reserve's target. As a result, many investors now expect the central bank to raise interest rates again next month.

gloss.inflation: the rate at which prices rise over time
gloss.core inflation: a measure of price rises that leaves out food and energy
gloss.target: a level that someone aims to reach
gloss.interest rate: the percentage charged for borrowing money
gloss.investor: a person who puts money into something to make a profit

items.title: PS5 owners report crashes after GTA VI launch
items.text: Some PlayStation 5 owners have reported shutdowns and graphics problems after playing Grand Theft Auto VI for several hours, GAMINGbible reported on 25 November. A user on X wrote that a console blackout had started and said his PS5 was using about 220 watts. The writer played about 100 hours on a launch-day console and had one crash. The site asked Rockstar Games and Sony for comment but had not received a reply. It said there could be many causes and that it was too soon to blame the game.

gloss.shut down: to stop working or switch off
gloss.launch: the first release of a product to the public
gloss.framerate: the number of images a game shows each second
gloss.blame: to say that someone or something is responsible for a problem
